chapters.title: Pushes and Pulls
chapters.topics: A push or a pull makes things start, stop, speed up, slow down, or change direction; bigger pushes make bigger changes; things that touch can push and pull; a ball rolling into another ball; ramps; stopping a moving thing; using a push to solve a problem (moving a heavy box).

chapters.title: What Things Are Made Of
chapters.topics: Describing materials by color, hardness, texture, bendiness, and whether they soak up water; sorting objects by their properties; choosing the right material for a job (a raincoat, a window); solids keep their shape and liquids take the shape of their container; a big thing can be built from small pieces and taken apart; heating and cooling can change things — some changes go back (ice, butter) and some do not (a cooked egg, burnt toast).

chapters.title: Sound Is a Wiggle
chapters.topics: Vibrating things make sound (a drum skin, a rubber band, your throat); sound can make things vibrate (rice on a drum); loud and soft, high and low; sound travels through air, water and solids; a string telephone; using sound to send a message (a bell, a whistle).

chapters.title: Light and Seeing
chapters.topics: You need light to see things; a dark room; light comes from the sun, fire, bulbs; some materials let light through, some let a little through, some block it and make shadows; mirrors bounce light; light can carry a signal (a flashlight blink, a lighthouse); the telescope collects light.

units.title: Living Things and Where They Live

chapters.title: What Plants and Animals Need
chapters.topics: Living and nonliving; plants need water, light and air to grow; animals need food, water, air and shelter; animals eat plants or other animals; plants and animals change their surroundings (a squirrel buries nuts, roots crack a sidewalk); people can change the land too and can take care of it.

chapters.title: Parents, Young and Habitats
chapters.topics: Young plants and animals look like their parents but not exactly; animals care for their young; body parts that help living things survive (beaks, claws, thorns, fur); many different kinds of living things live in different places (pond, prairie, forest, desert); a habitat gives what a living thing needs; pollinators and seeds that travel.

chapters.title: Weather and Seasons
chapters.topics: Weather is what the air is like today: sunny, cloudy, rainy, snowy, windy, hot, cold; measuring and charting weather; the four seasons in Illinois and how daylight changes; some weather is dangerous and forecasts help people get ready (tornado drill, snow day); dressing for the weather.

chapters.title: Sun, Moon and Stars
chapters.topics: The sun rises and sets in a pattern; the sun warms the ground, water and air; shade keeps things cooler; the moon can be seen in the day or the night and its shape seems to change in a pattern; stars come out at night; the telescope shows the moon's craters.

chapters.title: Land, Water and Change
chapters.topics: Earth has land and water — hills, rivers, lakes, oceans; maps show where they are; most water is in the ocean and is salty; water can be liquid or ice; wind and water change the shape of the land, fast (a flood) or slow (a river bend); people build walls and plant grass to slow it down.

chapters.title: Forces and Motion
chapters.topics: Forces have strength and direction; balanced forces and no change in motion, unbalanced forces and change; gravity pulls down; friction slows things; predicting motion from a pattern (a pendulum, a ball on a ramp); magnets push and pull without touching; static electricity; using forces to solve a problem (a magnetic latch).

chapters.title: Energy on the Move
chapters.topics: Faster means more energy; energy can be moved from place to place by sound, light, heat and electricity; collisions move energy from one object to another; energy stored in food, fuel and batteries; a circuit turns stored energy into light and motion; designing a device that changes energy from one form to another.

chapters.title: Particles Too Small to See
chapters.topics: Matter is made of particles too small to see; a gas is still matter (a balloon has weight); weight stays the same when matter changes shape, melts, dissolves or is mixed — measuring to prove it; identifying materials by properties (color, hardness, conductivity, solubility, magnetism); mixing can make new substances (baking soda and vinegar) or not (salt and water).

chapters.title: Waves, Light and Information
chapters.topics: Waves have amplitude and wavelength; waves in water and a jump rope; waves make objects move; light reflects off objects into our eyes and that is how we see; light bends when it passes through water and lenses; patterns like Morse code, binary and drum signals carry information; the wave bench.

chapters.title: Life Cycles and Traits
chapters.topics: Life cycles are different but all have birth, growth, reproduction and death (frog, butterfly, bean, oak); traits are inherited from parents and can also be changed by the environment (a plant in shade, a well-fed dog); variation among siblings; some traits give an advantage in finding mates or food.

chapters.title: Structures, Senses and Survival
chapters.topics: Plants and animals have internal and external structures for survival, growth and reproduction (roots, stems, thorns, heart, lungs, skin); the eye and how light lets animals see; senses send information to the brain and the brain responds; living in groups helps some animals survive; when the environment changes, some survive, some move, some die; fossils tell what lived long ago.

units.title: Ecosystems and the Flow of Energy

chapters.title: Where Plants Get Their Food
chapters.topics: Plants get the materials for growth mostly from air and water, not from the soil (van Helmont's tree); the sun's energy is stored in plants; animals get energy from the food they eat; food moves through the body to give energy, growth and repair; a healthy plate.

chapters.title: Food Webs and the Cycle of Matter

chapters.title: Earth in Space

Georgia; the Trail of Tears; the Seminole resistance; the Black Hawk War in Illinois; the war on the Bank; the Panic of 1837; the Whig Party; Martin Van Buren.

Austin; the Texas Revolution (the Alamo, San Jacinto), the Lone Star Republic and annexation; Polk, Oregon compromise; the U.S.-Mexican War and the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo; the Gadsden Purchase; Californios; the California Gold Rush, forty-niners, Chinese miners, impact on Native Californians.

chapters.title: The Changing American Identity
